verdict.detail: Measured 135 frames from 0 s to 4.5 s at 30 fps. Changed fraction 0.5597, mean change 0.775 levels per frame, longest static run 6 frames. 0 shot cuts, cadence mixed, flat-fill ratio 0.8387, grain 9.547.

numbers.method: ffmpeg extracts every frame in the window at native fps, scaled to 480 px wide. A Python driver (PIL and numpy, engine venv) loads frames one at a time and reports mean absolute grayscale difference against the frame before it, border MAD (outer 12%) and centre MAD (inner 50%), flat-fill ratio, outline density, grain (mean absolute Laplacian), and mean luma. It aggregates the top 8 quantized palette hexes and the mean 5-stop vertical gradient. A frame counts as changed when that difference is over 0.5 levels; a shot cut when it is over 22.0 levels. JavaScript turns the rows into changed fraction, mean change per frame and per second, longest static run, shot cuts, cadence, camera-vs-subject split, and a per-second motion curve. The prompt is built from those numbers only.

thresholds.changed_rule: A frame counts as changed when its mean absolute grayscale difference against the frame before it is over 0.5 levels. Encoded-video noise sits under 0.5, so a frame over that bar moved for real.
thresholds.shot_cut_rule: A frame counts as a shot cut when its mean absolute grayscale difference against the frame before it is over 22.0 levels. That is a full-scene change, not a moving subject.
thresholds.cadence_rule: static means no frame changed. on-1s means a change on nearly every frame (changed fraction at least 0.85). on-2s means a median gap of 2 frames between changed frames. on-3s means a median gap of 3. hold-and-pop means long static runs of at least 8 frames with a changed fraction under 0.5. Anything else is mixed.
thresholds.camera_rule: A step is camera-led when border MAD is over 0.5 and more than twice centre MAD. It is subject-led when centre MAD is over 0.5 and more than twice border MAD.
thresholds.verdict_rule: PASS when the window yields at least 2 frames, FAIL when it yields fewer. This command measures pace and style; it does not judge whether the pace is good, so a still window passes with a changed fraction of 0. The report carries the palette, flatness, outline, grain, and luminance bounds that --gate-image checks a generated still against.

context.meaning: Over 135 frames the video changes on 75 steps, a changed fraction of 0.5597. Mean change is 0.775 levels per frame, 23.249 levels per second. The longest static run is 6 frames (0.2 s). There are 0 shot cuts and cadence is mixed. The per-second curve names the motion in each second of the window.

limits: The numbers describe this window only. They do not describe the full video.
Frames are measured at 480 px wide. Small details under that scale are not in these numbers.

Mean absolute difference sees any pixel move, so a camera move reads as motion even when the subject holds still. The border and centre MADs split the two; read them before trusting the headline pace.
The palette is quantized to 5 bits per channel, so near colours merge into one hex. The gradient stops are medians across each row, so a wide figure can pull a stop toward the figure colour.
This command measures pace, palette, flatness, outline, grain, and gradient. It does not measure trajectories or easing; hme trace measures those.
